characterInteraction.description: Speaker 1 and Speaker 2 engage in a warm and humorous dialogue, highlighting their mutual respect and admiration. The conversation showcases their camaraderie and C. Mallesham's humble nature, emphasizing his dedication to his mother and his community.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The video emphasizes cultural significance and technological innovation in traditional craft, relevant to audiences interested in cultural heritage, technology, and inspirational stories.

keyMoments.changeDescription: A speaker takes the stage holding a beautifully woven saree, representing pride and accomplishment.
The speakers begin an engaging conversation filled with laughter and light-hearted moments.

narrativeProgression.description: The speaker introduces C. Mallesham and his family's profession.
The speaker displays a Pochampally saree made by C. Mallesham's family.
A photo of C. Mallesham's mother weaving is shown, highlighting her dedication.
The conversation shifts to the specifics of the traditional weaving process.
C. Mallesham emphasizes the time and physical strain involved in weaving a saree.
C. Mallesham's mother's plea to him to find a less strenuous alternative is recounted.
C. Mallesham decides to invent a machine to ease his mother's burden.
C. Mallesham's lack of formal education in engineering is acknowledged.
He describes his initial attempts at building the machine using basic materials.
He highlights the challenges and financial strain he faced.
C. Mallesham recounts the lack of support and ridicule he received.
Frustrated, he leaves his village for Hyderabad.
He takes a part-time job at a machine shop to observe and learn.
His dedication and persistence in studying the machines is evident.
He applies his learning to improve his own invention.
After seven years, he finally completes his machine.
His invention gains recognition and approval from fellow weavers.
C. Mallesham decides to share his invention with others.
He has already sold 500 machines.
Images showcasing the traditional and mechanized weaving process are displayed.
C. Mallesham has sold over 500 machines and continues to work on more.
He aims to produce and sell 3000 machines to meet the demand.
The speaker thanks C. Mallesham for sharing his story.

youtube_description:
http://www.inktalks.com One of the important initiatives of INK is its INK Fellows Program that brings together amazing young people, and showcases their work to the world. In this talk, INK Curator and Host Lakshmi Pratury speaks to INK Fellow C Mallesham from Andhra Pradesh in his local tongue, Telugu, to find out his amazing story. A story of how his weaver mother's agony drove him to invent a loom that would ease her pain at the same time allow her and others like her to keep spinning the silken threads of the famous Pochampalli saris.

ABOUT INK: INKtalks are personal narratives that get straight to the heart of issues in 18 minutes or less. We are committed to capturing and sharing breakthrough ideas, inspiring stories and surprising perspectives--for free!

Watch an INKtalk and meet the people who are designing the future--now. 

http://INKtalks.com

ABOUT C MALLESHAM: Making the adage, 'necessity is the mother of all inventions', ring true is C Mallesham, who, moved by his mother's suffering, innovated an automatic loom, that is also reviving the dying tradition of the Pochampally silk sari weaving. Laxmi Mallesham is now perhaps the happiest mother in Sharjipet, a village of handloom weavers in Andhra Pradesh. She, and many women weavers, is now free from pain and stress that consumed her for hours on the manual loom
youtube_title: C Mallesham: Mother of all innovations
